extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, defenders of religion (apologists), clergy, educated lay readers and translators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for proving the existence, wisdom and goodness of God by using modern observations and experiments in natural philosophy (with mathematical demonstrations where appropriate), aimed at convincing atheists and infidels and at making the material accessible to non-mathematicians. Also includes advice for translators and for presentation/organization of such works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only experimental observations and provable discoveries (no bare hypotheses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Methods we have made use of to prove the same, are only taken from the modern Observations, and provable Discoveries in Natural Philosophy, without laying down any bare Hypotheses; since in the Things of natural Knowledge we have no farther Foundation for Arguments than we can produce Experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments in natural philosophy intended to convince should be grounded on observable experiments and verifiable discoveries rather than speculative hypotheses. Where mathematical laws exist they may be used, but reliance should be on experimental demonstration so the proofs are accessible and convincing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer mathematical demonstration when appropriate, but adapt to reader's knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Able Mathematicians may think demonstrations should be more mathematical, but the author has deduced demonstrations as far as was possible by experiments and not by relying solely on established mathematical laws, so as to be better understood by those who know little or nothing of the Mathematicks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full mathematical proofs for specialists, but when addressing general readers present experiments, figures and intuitive demonstrations; include figures where helpful and only add mathematics when necessary to avoid incredibility. Balance rigor with accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'pious frauds' and dubious arguments for Divine attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the author passionately magnifies the Wisdom and Goodness of God he is such an Enemy to Pious Frauds, and to the supporting any of the Divine Attributes above-mentioned, by wrong, or even doubtful and precarious Argu­ments, that he uses none in confuting the Atheist and Sceptic but such as will bear even Mathematical Demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not appeal to dubious, rhetorical or logically weak arguments to defend theological claims; prefer arguments which can withstand demonstration and scrutiny. Omit or retract comments where the comment is wrong or repetitions are mere tautology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Scripture only as demonstrable evidence or to show divine authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manner of proving the Divinity of the Holy Scripture from natural Phenomena or Appearances ... is not supposed but proved; some Texts serve to shew the Wisdom and deep Knowledge in Nature of him who inspired them; others to convince that no mere human impostor could produce such writings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including scriptural citations, do so to illustrate how inspired authors show knowledge of nature or to support the claim of divine origin; do not assume scriptural authority a priori but argue for it where possible from observable phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnose causes of atheism and offer targeted remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to bring Atheists to Reason, it is necessary to enquire into the Causes and Remedies of Atheism; the first Cause is inordinate Self-love; other causes: inordinate Ambition, Ignorance, too great a Conceit of our own Wisdom, wrong manner of describing Nature, admitting no final Causes, disputation, inattention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attempting persuasion, identify psychological/intellectual causes behind denial (self-love, ambition, ignorance, pride, etc.) and address them directly with tailored remedies (humility, instruction, clearer methods, avoiding abuses of disputes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the abuse of academical disputes and sophistry
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sophistical Arguments of those Atheists, and the not only false, but horrible Consequences flowing from their Opinions, have been already fully expos'd ... The Abuse of Academical Disputes ... (Sections on remedies and abuse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not engage in or rely on purely technical scholastic disputes or sophistry that obscure plain facts; prefer clear experimental demonstrations and avoid unnecessarily abstruse disputation that alienates readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not deduce everything from hypotheses; use hypotheses appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: The Inconvenience of deducing every thing from an Hypothesis ... The Use of Hypotheses ... and Remedies thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses can be useful but should not serve as the sole foundation for conclusions about the natural world; whenever possible deduce conclusions from experiments and observed facts, and when hypotheses are used, be explicit about their provisional character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure expository contemplations with transitions and 'convictions' after observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contemplation contains Sections: Transition, Observations/Experiments, and 'Convictions from the foregoing Observations'—the book repeatedly transitions to a topic, lists experimental observations and then draws convictions from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize chapters into clear sections: introduce topic (transition), present experiments and observations (with figures/tables as needed), and then summarize explicit 'convictions' or conclusions derived from those observations to make the argumentative chain explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accessible vernacular and explain technical terms for wider usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: I write in the Low-Datch Tongue, to the End that I may be more useful to my own Country-men ... he is affected to express all his Technical Words or Terms of Art in his pure vernacular Tongue ... which has made me take Pains unknown to my indolent Temper throughout the whole Course of my Life till now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the vernacular to reach non-specialist audiences and take pains to render technical anatomical/physical/mathematical terms intelligibly; when native technical vocabulary differs from classical terminology, provide explanations and references for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include figures, tables and experimental details with references
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tables and Figures of my Author (which are very curious, and taken from the most valuable Anatomists and Philosophers) have been of good use to me, where there are proper References; ... I have therefore choſen to go on in that Way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide and reference figures/tables taken from reliable sources and include experimental procedures and outcomes so readers can verify or reproduce the demonstrations; cross-reference anatomical and experimental authorities where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be careful classifying unsettled scientific questions (honesty about uncertainty)
rubrics_metrics.description: This has made him a little too strict, it may be, in placing under the Class of Things unknown, the Motion of the Earth, and the Rest of the Planets about the Sun ... That he could not but wonder, extremely, that in the 29th Contemplation, the Motion of the Earth should be placed among Uncertainties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid prematurely labeling matters as unknown when evidence exists; be cautious and honest about the current status of knowledge, and acknowledge when treatises may err in classifying issues as uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: A single strong experimental fact may suffice; multiple demonstrations strengthen conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: If they proceed in the firſt Way, the strongest Proof will be of no Use to them; but if they fall into the latter, one single Fact weighed by a Mind ... may, by God's Blessing, convince them of their Error s. ... one Demonstration Proves as strongly as several, though more do strengthen the Conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that while repeated and varied demonstrations reinforce persuasion, sometimes a single clear, well-presented experiment can be decisive for a receptive mind; present both single strong facts and a body of supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: When translating or editing, omit unnecessary repetitions and erroneous glosses
rubrics_metrics.description: I have left several of the Texts out of this translation; but have retrenched none of his Glosses upon the particular Texts by him quoted, nor any of his Glorious Tautologies, in which he does so often call upon Atheists and Infidels; excepting where his Comment is wrong, or the Repetitions are too tedious, and, I hope, unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translators/editors should remove wrong comments and overly repetitive tautologies but preserve substantive glosses unless they are incorrect; trim tedious repetitions that do not add to conviction or clarity.
